column3: “In the south” is rendered “in the Negev,” and NASB supplies “It.”
“Has been told” is rendered “has been shown,” and NASB adds “still” and “she has caused.”
“Bent over … terrified” is rendered “so bewildered … so terrified”; NASB adds “I cannot hear … see.”
“A rider, a pair of horses” is rendered “riders, horsemen in pairs,” and “rider of a donkey” as “a train of donkeys.”
“A lion” is rendered “the lookout,” following a different reading.
“A rider, a man” is rendered “a troop of riders,” and NASB supplies “one.”
“Son of my threshing floor” is rendered “my afflicted of the threshing floor.”
“Dumah” is rendered “Edom,” following a different reading; “what of the night” becomes “how far gone is the night.”
The imperatives are reversed: “bring water” and “meet the fugitive.”
